title: Fragmentation and disk formation in high-mass star formation: The ALMA view of G351.77-0.54 at 0.06'' resolution
question: How does the high-mass hot core G351.77-0.54 fragment, and what are the kinematics, temperature structure and gravitational stability of its central disk-like structure at 0.06'' resolution?

data.sensitivity: 1 sigma rms 7 mJy/beam continuum; 30 mJy/beam line at 0.5 km/s

what.value: Large-scale 870 um gas mass of ~664 Msun at 1 kpc, 25 K

evidence.quote: From large-scale 870 $\mu$m continuum emission, (cite: leurini2011b) estimate a gas mass reservoir of $\sim$664 M$_{\odot}$ for a distance of 1 kpc and a temperature of 25 K.

what.value: Dust opacity kappa_438um = 6.3 cm2/g extrapolated to 1e6 cm-3

evidence.quote: we use a dust opacity $\kappa_{438\mu\rm{m}}=6.3$ cm$^2$ g$^{-1}$, extrapolated for densities of $10^6$ cm$^{-3}$ from (cite: ossenkopf1994)
we use as a reference $v_{\rm{lsr}}$ a value of $-3.63$ km s$^{-1}$ measured for CH$_3$CN$(12_2-11_2)v_8=1$ by (cite: leurini2011)

recipe.method: 438 um continuum image from line-avoided channels; peak positions, fluxes, Planck brightness temperatures; integrated flux within 4 sigma contours

recipe.goal: Derive dust column densities and masses
recipe.method: Optically thin dust emission following Hildebrand/Schuller
assumptions: gas-to-dust ratio 150; distance 2.2 kpc (1.0 kpc alternative)

recipe.method: CO(6-5) channel maps, red lobe integrated 25-42 km/s; CH3CN first-moment maps and pv cuts perpendicular to outflow, compared with Keplerian curves for 10 (4.5) Msun
Spherical Mdot = 4 pi r^2 rho v_in from red-shifted absorption, then scaled by disk solid angle
key_parameters: r ~80 AU, rho ~2.3e9 cm-3, v_in ~7.1 km/s

recipe.method: Pixel-by-pixel LTE fit of CH3CN and CH3(13)CN k-ladders, two components, hot component used
Q = c_s kappa/(pi G Sigma) per pixel with Keplerian Omega for 10 Msun, Sigma from the continuum; three temperature prescriptions
key_parameters: T = T_rot; T = 200 K; T ∝ r^-0.4 with 1400 K at 10 AU

evidence.quote:
approximate mass infall rates toward submm source #2 of $\dot{M}_{\rm{in}} \sim 1.6\times
10^{-3}$ M$_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$
disk infall rates around $\dot{M}_{\rm{disk,in}}\sim 0.8\times 10^{-3}$  M$_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$ at 2.2 kpc distance
We find very warm gas with temperatures largely around 1000 K with no steep gradient.
even the lowest values in the map derived with the temperature distribution are greater than $\sim$1.5

source densities of $\sim 1.8\times
10^4$ pc$^{-3}(2.0\times 10^5$ pc$^{-3}$) at 2.2(1) kpc distance

not_stated_but_needed: Channel/line selection and fitting ranges, priors and initial parameters for XCLASS pixel-by-pixel fits
Image size, cell size, deconvolver, masks and clean threshold
Continuum frequency used for the 438 um image (collapsed channels list)
How the Toomre Q uncertainties/epicyclic frequency were computed per pixel and inclination
Exact pv-cut width and position angle
score_reason: Single public dataset and a clear recipe, but imaging and XCLASS fit details are missing.
rediscovery_reason: Public data with numeric continuum and infall results; the recipe is reasonably clear.
